identification.summary: Oka Flood is Microsoft's name for a Russia-based influence-operations actor that Microsoft previously tracked as Storm-1679 [S4]. Microsoft calls Storm-1679 a prolific Russian influence actor whose main tactic is spoofed content that imitates reputable media outlets [S1]. Microsoft says the Paris 2024 Olympics were a primary objective since at least summer 2023, when the actor released the fake documentary 'Olympics Has Fallen' with AI-generated audio imitating Tom Cruise's voice [S1][S2]. In September 2024 Microsoft reported that Storm-1679 shifted from the French election and the Olympics to content targeting Kamala Harris [S3].
identification.firstObserved: Microsoft: Olympics-focused activity since at least summer 2023, with the fake documentary released on Telegram in June 2023 [S1][S2]. CheckFirst's related 'Operation Overload' reporting begins in 2023 [S5].
identification.notes: Microsoft name: Oka Flood (formerly Storm-1679), listed as a Russian influence-operations actor [S4]. Researchers outside Microsoft (ISD, as relayed by the AI Incident Database) treat Operation Overload, Matryoshka and Storm-1679 as one campaign [S8]. CheckFirst names the newsroom-flooding campaign Operation Overload [S5][S6]. These are separate analytic clusters whose equivalence Microsoft has not confirmed in the sources gathered. Microsoft reports Storm-1679 alongside Storm-1099 (Doppelganger) and Storm-1516, but tracks them as separate actors [S1][S3].

attribution.sponsor: Russia (Microsoft: Russia-affiliated influence actor) [S1][S4]. No sourced attribution to a specific Russian government organization.
attribution.confidence: Microsoft describes Storm-1679 as a Russian influence actor but does not name a state sponsor in the sources reviewed [S1][S3]. CheckFirst found that some email accounts used in Operation Overload were accessed from Russian residential IP addresses [S6][S9]. CheckFirst's CEO, Guillaume Kuster, called this 'a red flag' but 'not proof of anything', and said it was unclear who was behind the campaign or whether it was state-backed [S9]. No US government attribution was found.
attribution.basis: Microsoft Threat Analysis Center (MTAC) observation of content and amplification [S1][S2][S3]; Microsoft naming taxonomy [S4]; CheckFirst/Reset.Tech technical analysis of email infrastructure (Operation Overload cluster) [S5][S6].

objectives: Microsoft says the actor's goals were to damage the International Olympic Committee's reputation, create expectations of violence at the Paris 2024 Games, and discourage spectators from attending [S1][S2]. Earlier Russia-aligned celebrity-video content pushed the false narrative that President Zelensky abuses drugs [S1][S7]. In 2024 the actor turned to US election narratives that disparaged Kamala Harris [S3]. CheckFirst says the related Operation Overload campaign aims to drain fact-checker and newsroom resources and to push Kremlin narratives through trusted information channels [S5].

sectors: National governments and political leaders (France/Macron; US presidential campaign) [S1][S3]
Media, newsrooms and fact-checkers (impersonated or flooded) [S1][S5]
regions: Ukraine and Ukrainian refugee communities (earlier campaigns) [S1]
Germany (2025 federal election, per AI Incident Database reporting on Matryoshka/Operation Overload) [S8]
targeting.notes: Before spring 2024, content was mostly in English with some French, German and other European languages. French-language content increased in spring 2024 [S1]. Germany targeting comes from the Matryoshka/Operation Overload cluster, not from Microsoft reporting [S8].

capabilities.summary: Influence-operations tradecraft rather than network intrusion. Documented techniques include: AI-generated voice imitation of celebrities (Tom Cruise) in a feature-length fake documentary with spoofed Netflix branding and fake reviews attributed to the New York Times, Washington Post and BBC [S1][S2]; doctored Cameo videos bought from US celebrities and re-edited with anti-Ukraine messaging [S1][S7]; fake news clips and video 'press releases' impersonating Euronews, France 24, the CIA and France's DGSI [S1]; likely digitally generated graffiti images and false-flag impersonation of militant groups [S1]; and bot-amplified accounts and Telegram channels [S1]. In the September 2024 Harris content, Microsoft found the actor used actors and conventional editing rather than generative AI [S3]. The related Operation Overload cluster sends mass email to newsrooms (at least 71,000 emails reported by September 2024, with the volume having trebled since June) and uses 'content amalgamation' across X, Telegram and Russia-aligned sites [S5][S6][S9].

campaigns.name: 'Olympics Has Fallen' fake documentary
campaigns.summary: Released on Telegram with AI-generated Tom Cruise voice audio, spoofed Netflix branding and fabricated media reviews, to denigrate the IOC.

campaigns.name: Manipulated celebrity Cameo videos (anti-Zelensky)
campaigns.summary: MTAC reported in December 2023 that the activity began in July 2023: personalized Cameo clips from US celebrities were edited to suggest Zelensky abuses drugs, then amplified by Russian state media. Microsoft's 2024 Olympics report ties the Cameo tactic to Storm-1679.

campaigns.name: Operation Overload newsroom flooding (CheckFirst cluster)
campaigns.summary: Mass emails asking fact-checkers and newsrooms to verify fabricated content that impersonates media outlets, aimed at draining their resources. CheckFirst/Reset.Tech published their report in June 2024.

campaigns.name: Fear-of-violence content targeting Paris 2024
campaigns.summary: From fall 2023, graffiti images threatening Israeli attendees, plus fake Euronews and France 24 clips and fake CIA/DGSI video press releases suggesting terrorism and ticket returns.

campaigns.name: Pivot to US election (anti-Harris content)
campaigns.summary: Microsoft reported Storm-1679 shifted to Harris-focused content, including a fabricated Times Square billboard video on Telegram that drew over 100,000 views within hours. Operation Overload was also reported to be targeting the US election.

campaigns.name: Matryoshka/Operation Overload activity (USAID video; German election)
campaigns.summary: Researchers tied a viral fake video claiming USAID paid celebrities to visit Ukraine to Matryoshka (also called Operation Overload and Storm-1679). The cluster was also reported active around Germany's February 2025 election.

diamond.adversary: Russia-based influence actor tracked by Microsoft as Oka Flood (formerly Storm-1679); no named sponsoring organization in the sources [S1][S4].
diamond.capability: AI voice cloning, doctored celebrity videos, spoofed media branding, fake press releases from intelligence agencies, false-flag militant imagery, and mass email to newsrooms (Operation Overload cluster) [S1][S3][S5].
diamond.infrastructure: Telegram channels (e.g., 'Olympics Has Fallen'), bot-amplified social-media accounts, Cameo purchases, X accounts and Russia-aligned websites; email accounts accessed from Russian residential IPs (Operation Overload) [S1][S5][S6].
diamond.victim: IOC and Paris 2024 Games, French and US political leaders, impersonated media organizations and agencies, fact-checkers and newsrooms, and Western social-media audiences [S1][S3][S5].
diamond.socioPolitical: Microsoft says the aims are to denigrate the IOC, create fear of violence at Paris 2024, undermine support for Ukraine and influence the 2024 US election [S1][S3].
diamond.technology: Exploits audience trust in established media brands and celebrity likenesses, cheap generative-AI audio, and the verification workload of fact-checking organizations [S1][S5].

gaps: Microsoft's primary MTAC report PDF (June 2024) and the On the Issues blog post could not be opened (host unreachable). Details come from Microsoft's Security Insider page [S1] and press coverage [S2].
Microsoft's September 2024 MTAC election report was not located. Harris-related details come from TechTarget coverage [S3].
The imported record calls Storm-1679 an Internet Research Agency spinoff. No Microsoft or other reliable source gathered confirms this, so it is excluded.

Cluster equivalence: ISD (via AI Incident Database) equates Operation Overload, Matryoshka and Storm-1679 [S8]. Microsoft's own publications reviewed do not state this. Treat CheckFirst's Operation Overload findings (email volume, Russian IPs) as possibly overlapping, not as confirmed Oka Flood activity.

December 2023 press coverage of the Cameo operation described the actor as unnamed and Russia-aligned [S7]. The attribution to Storm-1679 rests on Microsoft's 2024 Olympics reporting as summarized in [S1].

CheckFirst pages and the ISD report could not be fetched (blocked). Their content was taken from search excerpts, and the exact publication date of the CheckFirst US-election follow-up is approximate [S6].
No government attribution (US, French or German) to Oka Flood/Storm-1679 by name was found.
No sourced information on organizational structure, funding, personnel, or 2025-2026 activity under the Oka Flood name.

implications.jipoe: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. STEP 1 (operational environment): The information environment counts as key terrain. That includes Telegram, X, short-form video platforms, the brands of trusted Western media and agencies (CIA, DGSI, BBC, France 24), and fact-checking organizations [S1][S5]. STEP 2 (effects): The actor imitates trusted brands and celebrity voices cheaply, so audiences and newsrooms face content that looks authoritative. Verification capacity is the friendly vulnerability the actor exploits [S1][S5]. STEP 3 (adversary model): Pick a high-visibility event (Olympics, election). Produce spoofed media or a fake press release that hints at violence or scandal. Seed it on Telegram and amplify it with bots. Then email newsrooms asking them to 'verify' it [S1][S3][S5]. STEP 4 (COAs): The most likely COA (MLCOA) is fabricated news clips or fake official statements around major Western events and elections that discredit leaders and support for Ukraine [S1][S3]. The most dangerous COA (MDCOA) is a fabricated 'official' threat warning (for example, a spoofed CIA or allied intelligence press release) released during a real crisis or a major event with a US military presence, which would trigger panic, force-protection confusion or misdirected public affairs responses [S1]. Candidate indicators: content carrying spoofed logos of agencies or outlets that is absent from their official channels; new Telegram channels pushing event-specific fear narratives; bursts of verification-request emails to press and public affairs offices [S1][S5].
implications.jcc2: Analyst assessment derived from cited sources; validate before use. (1) Situational awareness: Track impersonation of US government and DoD brands alongside media spoofing, since the actor has faked CIA press releases [S1]. Give public affairs and IO cells a shared picture of active fabricated narratives. (2) Authorities: This is an influence actor with no sourced network-intrusion activity. Responses fall mainly under IO, public affairs and interagency (State GEC successor functions, FBI FITF) lanes rather than DCO. Confirm authorities before any cyberspace response. (3) Mission assurance: Expect fabricated threat content around large events and exercises with a US presence. Prepare rapid authoritative messaging to prevent operational disruption [S1]. (4) Coordination: Share indicators with platform operators and allied counterparts (France, Germany) that are dealing with the same campaigns. Do not merge vendor clusters (Storm-1679, Operation Overload, Matryoshka) in reporting without noting the source of each [S5][S8].
